The transport networks now have a proof of an imposed response: increasing the paired
temperature gradient cannot reduce the predicted heat flux when the other network inputs
stay fixed ([all 20 members of each ensemble pass both heat-flux monotonicity properties, with derivative lower bound zero over the full training box]{.claim}[C-247](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-247){.cid .st-measured}). This is a statement about the networks. It does not
establish that they reproduce the underlying physics where TGLF itself is non-monotone.

The checks take two routes. The first inspects the saved weights and confirms that every
path from the selected gradient to its heat-flux output has non-negative gain. The second
asks the bound-propagation library to bound the derivative. Each activation slope stays
between zero and one; letting those slopes vary independently gives a larger domain that
contains every state reachable within the training box. Both routes agree.

Before proving each member, its exported predictions and derivative calculation are checked
against the JAX model on random-box and held-out inputs. The certificates bind the model,
box, property, verifier source and numerical results. A negative-path regression checks that
a deliberately decreasing derivative is detected.

The proof belongs to the saved model and its declared property. The deployed model and
guard are unchanged, and the MAST-U reference limitation remains. The owner's final M4
certification review is still ahead.

## What's next

V5 will bound the outputs of transport, EC and pedestal models. Those bounds, calibration,
remaining coupled checks and guard integration are needed before the certification review.
